title: Russian forces launch a major assault on Avdiivka in Donetsk Oblast
body:
On 10 October 2023 Ukraine's General Staff reported that up to three Russian battalions, totalling more than 2,000 soldiers and supported by tanks and armoured vehicles, had intensified operations against the town of Avdiivka in Donetsk Oblast. The Kyiv Independent described the assault as coming after months of a relatively static siege and as involving armour, artillery and air strikes. Russia also carried out heavy strikes on the town, and more of the remaining residents left.

Vitalii Barabash, head of the Avdiivka City Military Administration, said Russia had never before used such an amount of equipment there. On 11 October the General Staff said Ukrainian forces repelled 10 attacks against Avdiivka and eight more east of Stepove and southeast of Sieverne. On 12 October it reported 10 further unsuccessful attacks in the Avdiivka direction. The General Staff reported close to 1,000 Russian casualties per day on 11 and 12 October, about double the earlier average. Those figures are Ukrainian claims. President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Telegram that Ukrainian forces were holding their positions.

Avdiivka has been on the front line since 2014, and Russia began escalating attacks on it in July 2022. The Institute for the Study of War assessed that attacks on the flanks suggested an aim to encircle the town, while analysts cited by the Kyiv Independent said full encirclement would require units and freedom of action that Russia lacked. By October 2023 the town was largely destroyed and depopulated.
